structured.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
structured.naturalResources: cobalt, copper, niobium, tantalum, petroleum, industrial and gem diamonds, gold, silver, zinc, manganese, tin, uranium, coal, hydropower, timber
structured._source: wikidata (CC0); landBorders + naturalResources from CIA World Factbook (public domain)

prose.hook: Straddling the equator in Central Africa, this is the second-largest country in Africa and the largest in sub-Saharan Africa, dominated by a low-lying central basin of dense tropical rainforest ringed by eastern highlands. The Congo River running through it is conceded to be the deepest river in the world, with its greatest depth estimated between 220 and 250 meters, though its speed, cataracts, and rapids have made much of it impossible to measure precisely. A narrow strip of land along the lower river is the country's only outlet to the South Atlantic.
prose.physicalGeography: The country's interior is a vast, low-lying plateau forming the central Congo basin, bordered by mountains in the east. It sits in Central Africa, northeast of Angola, with the basin's rainforest giving way to highland terrain toward the eastern frontier.
prose.climate: The climate is tropical, hot and humid in the equatorial river basin, but cooler and drier in the southern highlands and cooler and wetter in the eastern highlands. Wet and dry seasons run on opposite schedules north and south of the equator. Periodic droughts affect the south, the Congo River floods seasonally, and active volcanism along the Great Rift Valley in the east is a serious hazard: Nyiragongo, at 3,470 meters, threatens the city of Goma and its quarter-million residents with lava that can travel up to 100 km/hr, while its neighbor Nyamuragira is Africa's most active volcano.
prose.economy: This is a very poor but resource-rich country holding the world's second-largest rainforest, with mining as its economic backbone — copper, cobalt, gold, diamonds, coltan, zinc, tin, and tungsten feed industries in mineral processing, metal products, textiles, footwear, and cement, alongside timber and commercial ship repair. Trade with China's extractive sector has grown even as government investment has fallen sharply and the country faces a widening current account deficit and rising public debt. Refined copper, cobalt, copper ore, raw copper, and crude petroleum are its leading exports.
prose.peopleAndCulture: More than 200 African ethnic groups call the country home, most of them Bantu; the four largest — Mongo, Luba, Kongo, and the Hamitic Mangbetu-Azande — together make up about 45% of the population. Christianity dominates religious life, split between Roman Catholic and Protestant adherents alongside other Christian denominations, with smaller communities following the Kimbanguist church, Islam, and syncretic or indigenous beliefs.
